report.summary: Chunk 3 of 8: harness.py lines 241-345 — implements tier1 evaluation, aggregation, and whole-repo text generation.
risks: run_tier1 | medium | The function modifies dirnames in os.walk to skip ignored dirs; side-effect on the walk is safe but could be surprising. | Confirm that _IGNORE_DIRS is properly defined and that mutating dirnames is intended.

handoff.purpose: Implements tier1 evaluation loop, result aggregation, and whole-repo text generation.

symbols.name: _tier1_aggregate
symbols.note: Aggregates per-task rows into summary stats: n_tasks, mean_recall, mean_compression, n_slice_recall_misses, missed_ids.

symbols.name: run_tier1
symbols.note: Main entry point for Tier 1 evaluation. Accepts optional task list, builds index cache, evaluates each task, returns summary dict with per_task, errored, by_provenance, etc.

symbols.name: _whole_repo_text
symbols.note: Walks a repo root, concatenates source files with headers; returns (text, truncated). cap_chars=None means untruncated.

claims.why: The function initializes truncated = False and only sets it to True inside the loop (not shown) when cap_chars is reached; if cap_chars is None the loop never sets truncated, so it remains False.

claims.text: ``cap_chars=None`` (the new default) walks the ENTIRE repo untruncated -- the TRUE size of the baseline.
claims.why: The code shows the function signature with cap_chars: int | None = None and the loop, but the actual truncation logic (if cap_chars is not None) is not in this chunk; we cannot confirm that None disables truncation, though the comment says so.

claims.text: ``tier == "quarantine"`` tasks are counted in ``n_quarantine_tasks`` and reported inside ``by_provenance``, but never inside a go/no-go figure.
claims.why: The return dict includes 'n_quarantine_tasks' computed as n - n_primary, and 'by_provenance' is computed from 'healthy' tasks; there is no 'go/no-go' field in the return, so quarantine tasks are excluded from any such figure.

claims.text: A single unresolvable task (bad ``repo`` label, or a target no longer in the index -- the quarantined-mint-task crash this guards against) is caught here too, not just inside ``eval_task_tier1``.
claims.why: The loop catches ValueError/OSError from resolve_task_repo or cached_index and appends _task_error_row, then continues; this is the guard described.

claims.text: ERRORED rows land in both ``per_task`` (never silently dropped -- 'a degraded measurement is reported, never silent') and the dedicated ``errored`` list, and are excluded from ``by_provenance`` (every mean/recall/compression aggregate) -- see ``_by_provenance``'s docstring.
claims.why: errored = [t for t in per_task if 'error' in t] collects them; healthy = [t for t in per_task if 'error' not in t and not t.get('focus_withheld')]; by_provenance is called only with healthy, so errored rows are excluded from aggregates.

claims.text: ``n_tasks``/``n_primary_tasks``/``n_quarantine_tasks`` remain simple total-attempted counts over label alone (unaffected by error status, and therefore byte-identical to before this existed for any store with zero errored tasks); ``n_errored_tasks`` is new and additive.
claims.why: n_tasks = len(per_task) (includes errored), n_primary counts based on label_tier, n_quarantine = n - n_primary; these are unaffected by error status. n_errored_tasks is computed separately.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD (lane A1): the fence fail-closed on the task's own focus file -- not a resolution error (excluded above), not a recall outcome either. Excluded from `healthy` (therefore from every mean/miss count in by_provenance) same as errored rows, and separately counted/named so it is reported, never silently folded into either a pass or a miss.
claims.why: focus_withheld = [t for t in per_task if t.get('focus_withheld')]; healthy excludes focus_withheld; return includes n_focus_withheld and focus_withheld_ids.

claims.text: Defaulted so pre-provenance task dicts (e.g. ad-hoc test fixtures that predate this schema) still group as 'hand_reachable'/'primary' -- additive, byte-identical aggregation for callers who never adopted the new fields.
claims.why: The return dict uses task.get('label_provenance', 'hand_reachable') and task.get('tier', 'primary'), providing defaults.

observations.what: Function _whole_repo_text modifies dirnames in os.walk to skip ignored dirs; this is safe but may be surprising.
The docstring for run_tier1 references _by_provenance's docstring, which is not in this chunk; cannot verify the claim about its behavior.
